en: Jose Rizal discovered a rare flying lizard species that scientists later named Draco rizali in his honor.
The Philippine government officially declared Arnis as the national martial art and sport to preserve indigenous self-defense techniques.
The Chief Justice of the Supreme Court is the specific official required to administer the oath of office to the President.
The ancient Ifugao people carved the Banaue Rice Terraces entirely by hand using simple tools, without modern irrigation blueprints.
The ancient Baybayin writing system is unique because every single character represents a complete syllable instead of just one letter.
Dr. Fe del Mundo invented a bamboo incubator that kept premature babies warm in rural areas without electricity.
The name of the famous Ati-Atihan festival literally translates to making believe to be Atis, honoring the indigenous Aeta people.
The Philippine Constitution uniquely mandates that the State must protect and promote the right to a balanced and healthful ecology.
Marcela Agoncillo and her daughter sewed the first Philippine flag, which was officially unfurled during the 1898 independence declaration in Cavite.
The traditional bayanihan practice literally involved an entire community physically carrying a family's entire nipa hut on bamboo poles to a new location.
Juan Luna’s massive painting Spoliarium won the highest first gold medal at the prestigious Madrid Exposition of Fine Arts in 1884.
The Barong Tagalog is traditionally worn untucked because Spanish colonizers originally mandated it to easily spot any hidden weapons underneath.
